reason: The finding asks for no change. Its idea of skipping the 12:04Z run because the snapshot is fresh is already built into the timer. CONTEXT l.2530-2531 says timer 2f0d1fa1 runs the E10 P1 only when the newest e10_watch snapshot is more than 2 h 30 min old, and l.2748 carries that timer over to 2e87e414 with the 'same schedule'. The newest snapshot is experiments/e10_watch/20260927T1101Z.txt, so at 12:04Z it is 63 min old and the tick does nothing. At 15:04Z it is 4 h 03 min old and the tick runs. That is after the 43/44 read, whose latest edge is the 14:28:22Z header or the 14:40Z fallback. So R16-A7 (first full P1 after the read) already happens with no edit. Editing a session timer to log 'deferred' only adds a chance of breaking it. The cadence half ('return to the hh:04 grid') is out of date and now wrong. At 11:08Z the user issued E10 v3 (CONTEXT l.2917-2926): the trigger is any public notebook at 0.955 or better, handled 'as fast as possible'. research/wf_ideas_v4/e10v3/build_watch.notes.md shows an hourly v3 watch being built from 11:12Z. Ties at the same score go to the earlier submission, and 74 teams sit at exactly 0.955 in the 11:01Z snapshot. Waiting for the read (up to ~14:40Z) and then going back to a 3-hour grid would delay a v3 trigger, the one case with real score upside. Round-17 skeptics already made this point (v_hyp_post_r8_plan_r17p-f3.json point 3, r17p-f6.json cadence). The 'noise' claim is weak. e10_snapshot makes 8 read-only CLI calls and no ListSubmissions ('fetch: 8 OK'), so it cannot touch poll.log or the read trigger. An extra run costs one diff file. Uncertainty: I could not list the main session's crons to confirm that 2e87e414 kept the 2.5 h staleness clause. 'Same schedule' implies it did. It does not matter either way: an extra read-only snapshot is harmless and v3 wants more checks, not fewer.
fix: Leave timer 2e87e414 alone: at 12:04Z its staleness gate will skip the run. Log it at most as info: '12:04Z E10 tick: newest snapshot 11:01Z < 2.5 h, no-op by rule'. Take the cadence from E10 v3, not from R16-A7's 3-hour grid. Run the hourly v3 watch as soon as it is built (research/wf_ideas_v4/e10v3/), including through the 43/44 read window, since it makes no ListSubmissions call. Also run a P1 at once after the read if the v3 watch is not live yet. Keep the 3-hour hh:04 timer only as a backup.
realistic_gain: 0 on the score. As written, deferring and then going back to the 3-hour grid risks a small loss: 1-3 h of extra delay to an E10 v3 trigger, which costs tie position at 0.955. The part that stands (no 12:04Z run needed) is already automatic.
